newsitem.title: BELGIUM: MEPs to approve double pricing for goods.
newsitem.headline: MEPs to approve double pricing for goods.

text.p: The European Parliament is due on February 19 to approve an EU directive which will force shops to indicate the price of goods both by item and by weight.
This will mean, for example, that a packet of cheddar cheese will be labelled to show the price of that individual packet and the price of a kilogramme of cheddar.
For six months before and after the introduction of the European single currency, labels will also show the price of the item in euros.
"I'm in favour of giving consumers the best possible information," British Socialist Philip Whitehead, from the parliament's environment and consumer affairs committee, told Reuters.
Last month the committee adopted a report on the draft directive -- COM(95)276 -- which reintroduces 20 amendments previously rejected by the Council of Ministers in its common position on the text.
One of the most important amendments concerns the arrangements for small retailers.
Parliament thinks small retailers should have six years to adapt to the new rules, by which time the European Commission should have produced clear details of how much it will cost.
The Council favours excluding small retailers from the directive altogether.
"My priority is to have a sufficient period of time for the implementation of these measures and a review of the cost of their introduction," Whitehead said.
"One of the things that gests the Commission a bad name is churning out proposals without costing them."
The proposal needs the support of both ministers and MEPs to become law.
Whitehead predicted parliament and Council would have to go through tough conciliation talks before a reasonable compromise could be reached.
